title: Health (5th Grade)
description: Health (5th Grade) practice - 133 questions, including Delaware-mandated sexual extortion prevention content (Delaware Code Section 4163)

questions.question: Which food group do apples, bananas, and oranges belong to?
questions.correctAnswer: Fruits
questions.explanation: Fruits grow on plants and trees, and they are full of vitamins and fiber that help your body stay healthy.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: fruits are nature's sweet snacks!

questions.question: Which food group do carrots, broccoli, and spinach belong to?
questions.correctAnswer: Vegetables
questions.explanation: Vegetables grow in gardens and fields. They give your body vitamins, minerals, and fiber.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: veggies grow in the garden - eat your greens!

questions.question: Which food group do bread, rice, and pasta belong to?
questions.correctAnswer: Grains
questions.explanation: Grains come from plants like wheat and rice. They give your body energy to run, play, and learn.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: grains give you energy to run and play!

questions.question: Which food group do milk, cheese, and yogurt belong to?
questions.correctAnswer: Dairy
questions.explanation: Dairy foods come from milk. They are rich in calcium, which builds strong bones and teeth.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: dairy builds strong bones!

questions.question: Which food group do chicken, beans, and eggs belong to?
questions.correctAnswer: Protein
questions.explanation: Protein foods help your body build and repair muscles. Chicken, beans, and eggs are all good sources.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: protein builds strong muscles!

questions.question: What does protein help your body do?
questions.correctAnswer: Build and repair muscles
distractors: Help you see in the dark
questions.explanation: Protein builds muscles and repairs body tissues.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: protein is the builder for muscles!

questions.question: Why is calcium important for kids?
questions.correctAnswer: It builds strong bones and teeth
distractors: It makes your hair grow longer
questions.explanation: Calcium from milk and other foods makes bones and teeth strong.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: calcium is the bone builder!

questions.question: Which of these is the healthiest drink?
questions.correctAnswer: Water
questions.explanation: Water hydrates your body without sugar.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: water is the best drink of all!

questions.question: Why is eating a variety of foods important?
questions.correctAnswer: Different foods give your body different nutrients
distractors: It makes meals more fun only
questions.explanation: Your body needs many nutrients, and no single food has them all.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: eat a rainbow - every color brings different nutrients!

questions.question: What is a whole grain?
questions.correctAnswer: A grain that keeps all its parts, like whole wheat bread
questions.explanation: Whole grains keep the bran, germ, and endosperm, with fiber and nutrients.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: whole grains keep all their good parts!

questions.question: Which snack is healthiest?
questions.correctAnswer: An apple with peanut butter
questions.explanation: An apple with peanut butter gives fiber, vitamins, and protein.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: apple plus peanut butter is a super snack!

questions.question: What does fiber do for your body?
questions.correctAnswer: It helps digestion and keeps you feeling full
distractors: It gives you energy right away
questions.explanation: Fiber from fruits, vegetables, and whole grains helps your digestion.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: fiber keeps your tummy happy!

questions.question: Why should you limit sugary drinks?
questions.correctAnswer: They have lots of sugar and can harm your teeth and health
questions.explanation: Sugary drinks add sugar without nutrients and can cause cavities.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: sugary drinks are a cavity trap!

questions.question: How many servings of fruits and vegetables should kids aim for each day?
questions.correctAnswer: Five servings
questions.explanation: Health experts suggest about five servings of fruits and vegetables a day.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: five a day keeps you strong and healthy!

questions.question: What vitamin helps your body fight sickness?
questions.correctAnswer: Vitamin C
questions.explanation: Vitamin C, found in oranges and peppers, supports the immune system.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: vitamin C is your germ-fighting helper!

questions.question: Which food is a good source of vitamin C?
questions.correctAnswer: Oranges
questions.explanation: Oranges, strawberries, and peppers are packed with vitamin C, which helps your immune system fight germs.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: oranges are vitamin C champions!

questions.question: Why is breakfast called the most important meal of the day?
questions.correctAnswer: It gives you energy after sleeping all night
questions.explanation: Breakfast refuels your body after the night and helps you focus.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: breakfast fuels your morning brain!

questions.question: What is a balanced meal?
questions.correctAnswer: A meal with foods from different food groups
distractors: A meal with only one food
A meal with lots of dessert
questions.explanation: A balanced meal includes grains, protein, fruits, vegetables, and dairy.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: a balanced plate has a little of everything!

questions.question: Which of these has the most added sugar?
questions.correctAnswer: A can of soda
questions.explanation: One can of soda can hold about 10 teaspoons of added sugar, far more than an apple or a carrot, which have only natural sugars.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: soda is sugar water in a can!

questions.question: Why is it important to drink water during exercise?
questions.correctAnswer: To replace the water your body loses in sweat
questions.explanation: Sweating loses water, and drinking replaces it so you do not get dehydrated.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: sweat out water, drink it back in!

questions.question: What does your heart do?
questions.correctAnswer: It pumps blood around your body
questions.explanation: The heart is a muscle that pumps blood to every part of your body.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: your heart is a pump that never rests!

questions.question: What do your lungs do?
questions.correctAnswer: They help you breathe in oxygen and breathe out carbon dioxide
questions.explanation: Lungs take in oxygen from the air and send it into your blood.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: your lungs are breathing balloons!

questions.question: What does your brain do?
questions.correctAnswer: It controls your body and helps you think and learn
questions.explanation: The brain is the control center for thinking, feeling, and moving.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: your brain is the boss of your whole body!

questions.question: What do your bones do?
questions.correctAnswer: They support your body and protect your organs
questions.explanation: Bones give your body shape and protect organs like the brain and heart.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: bones are your body's strong frame!

questions.question: What do muscles do?
questions.correctAnswer: They help your body move
questions.explanation: Muscles pull on bones to make your body move.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: muscles pull your bones to move you!

questions.question: How many bones does an adult have?
questions.explanation: An adult has 206 bones. Kids have more, and some fuse as they grow.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: 206 bones hold you up!

questions.question: What does your stomach do?
questions.correctAnswer: It breaks down food with acids and churning
questions.explanation: The stomach mixes food with acids to start digestion.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: your stomach is a food-mixing machine!

questions.question: What is the job of your skin?
questions.correctAnswer: It protects your body and helps you feel things
questions.explanation: Skin covers and protects you and senses touch, heat, and cold.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: skin is your body's shield!

questions.question: What do red blood cells do?
questions.correctAnswer: They carry oxygen around your body
questions.explanation: Red blood cells pick up oxygen in the lungs and deliver it to cells.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: red blood cells are oxygen delivery trucks!

questions.question: What do white blood cells do?
questions.correctAnswer: They fight germs and sickness
questions.explanation: White blood cells attack germs that make you sick.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: white blood cells are your germ fighters!

questions.question: What is your pulse?
questions.correctAnswer: The beating of your heart that you can feel in your wrist or neck
questions.explanation: Each heartbeat sends a pulse of blood through your arteries.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: your pulse is your heartbeat you can feel!

questions.question: Why does your heart beat faster when you exercise?
questions.correctAnswer: Your muscles need more oxygen, so your heart pumps faster
questions.explanation: Exercise needs more oxygen, so the heart works harder to deliver it.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: exercise makes your heart pump faster to feed your muscles!

questions.question: What is the largest organ in your body?
questions.correctAnswer: Your skin
questions.explanation: Skin is the largest organ, covering your whole body.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: skin is your biggest organ!

questions.question: What does the spine do?
questions.correctAnswer: It supports your body and protects the nerves inside
questions.explanation: The spine is a column of bones that holds you up and guards the spinal cord.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: your spine is your body's strong pole!

questions.question: How does your body get energy from food?
questions.correctAnswer: Digestion breaks food down and cells use the nutrients for energy
distractors: Your stomach burns food like a fire
questions.explanation: Digestion turns food into nutrients your cells use for energy.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: food becomes fuel after digestion!

questions.question: Why should you wash your hands before eating?
questions.correctAnswer: To remove germs that could make you sick
distractors: To make your hands smell nice
questions.explanation: Handwashing removes germs before they can get into your body.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: wash away the germs before you eat!

questions.question: How long should you scrub your hands with soap?
questions.correctAnswer: About 20 seconds
questions.explanation: Scrubbing for 20 seconds, about the time to sing 'Happy Birthday' twice, removes germs.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: scrub for 20 seconds - sing Happy Birthday twice!

questions.question: How often should you brush your teeth?
questions.correctAnswer: Twice a day
questions.explanation: Brushing twice a day removes plaque and helps prevent cavities.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: brush twice a day for a bright smile!

questions.question: Why should you floss your teeth?
questions.correctAnswer: To clean between teeth where a brush cannot reach
distractors: To make your breath smell nice only
questions.explanation: Floss removes food and plaque from between teeth.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: floss reaches where the brush cannot!

questions.question: What should you do when you cough or sneeze?
questions.correctAnswer: Cover your mouth with your elbow or a tissue
questions.explanation: Covering your cough stops germs from spreading to others.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: cough into your elbow, not your hands!

questions.question: How many hours of sleep do kids aged 9 to 12 need each night?
questions.correctAnswer: 9 to 12 hours
questions.explanation: Kids need 9 to 12 hours of sleep to grow and learn well.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: 9 to 12 hours of sleep helps you grow and learn!

questions.question: Why is sleep important?
questions.correctAnswer: It helps your body grow and your brain learn and remember
questions.explanation: During sleep, your body grows and your brain stores what you learned.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: sleep is when your brain files away the day!

questions.question: What should you do before bed to sleep well?
questions.correctAnswer: Turn off screens and relax
questions.explanation: Screens and sugar make it harder to fall asleep.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: screens off, calm on - good sleep follows!

questions.question: Why should you wear sunscreen?
questions.correctAnswer: To protect your skin from harmful sun rays
questions.explanation: Sunscreen blocks UV rays that can burn and damage skin.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: sunscreen is a shield against sunburn!

questions.question: What should you wear to protect your head when riding a bike?
questions.correctAnswer: A helmet
questions.explanation: A helmet protects your brain if you fall.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: a helmet protects your brain - always wear one!

questions.question: Why is it important to look both ways before crossing the street?
questions.correctAnswer: To check for cars coming from either direction
distractors: To see the traffic light only
questions.explanation: Cars can come from either direction, and looking both ways - then looking left again - makes sure the road is clear before you step off the curb.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: look left, look right, then cross!

questions.question: What should you do if a stranger offers you a ride?
questions.correctAnswer: Say no and tell a trusted adult
questions.explanation: Never go with a stranger; tell a parent, teacher, or other trusted adult.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: strangers offering rides mean say no and tell an adult!

questions.question: Why should you never share a toothbrush?
questions.correctAnswer: Germs can spread from one person's mouth to another
distractors: It is against the rules only
questions.explanation: Sharing a toothbrush can spread germs and sickness.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: your toothbrush is yours alone - germs hitchhike!

questions.question: How often should you visit the dentist?
questions.correctAnswer: About twice a year
questions.explanation: Regular checkups catch problems early.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: twice a year keeps your smile in check!

questions.question: What is the best way to stay healthy when someone near you is sick?
questions.correctAnswer: Wash your hands often and avoid touching your face
questions.explanation: Germs get in through your eyes, nose, and mouth. Clean hands and keeping hands away from your face block their way in.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: wash hands, hands off your face!

questions.question: How much physical activity should kids get each day?
questions.correctAnswer: At least 60 minutes
questions.explanation: Health experts say kids need at least 60 minutes of activity daily.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: 60 minutes of play every day keeps you strong!

questions.question: What is a good warm-up before exercise?
questions.correctAnswer: Light movement like walking or gentle stretching
distractors: Sprinting as fast as you can
questions.explanation: Warming up prepares muscles and helps prevent injury.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: warm up gently before you play hard!

questions.question: Why is stretching good for you?
questions.correctAnswer: It keeps muscles flexible and helps prevent injury
questions.explanation: Stretching keeps muscles loose and flexible.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: stretching keeps muscles bendy and safe!

questions.question: What does the word 'aerobic' exercise mean?
questions.correctAnswer: Exercise that gets your heart pumping, like running or swimming
questions.explanation: Aerobic exercise raises your heart rate and breathing.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: aerobic means heart-pumping movement!

questions.question: Which activity is best for building strong bones?
questions.correctAnswer: Jumping, running, and other weight-bearing activities
questions.explanation: Activities where your feet hit the ground strengthen bones.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: jumping and running build strong bones!

questions.question: Why should you cool down after exercise?
questions.correctAnswer: To let your heart rate slow down gradually
questions.explanation: Cooling down helps your body return to normal safely.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: cool down slowly - let your heart settle!

questions.question: What should you do if a muscle hurts during exercise?
questions.correctAnswer: Stop and rest, and tell an adult if it keeps hurting
distractors: Keep going as hard as you can
questions.explanation: Pain is a signal to stop and rest.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: pain means stop and rest - listen to your body!

questions.question: How does exercise help your brain?
questions.correctAnswer: It improves focus, memory, and mood
distractors: It does not affect the brain
questions.explanation: Activity sends more oxygen to the brain and improves learning.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: moving your body sharpens your brain!

questions.question: Which of these is a team sport?
questions.correctAnswer: Soccer
questions.explanation: Soccer is played by a team working together.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: soccer is a team game!

questions.question: What is good sportsmanship?
questions.correctAnswer: Playing fair, respecting others, and handling winning and losing well
questions.explanation: Good sportsmanship means fair play and respect.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: play fair and respect everyone - that is sportsmanship!

questions.question: Why is it important to drink water before, during, and after exercise?
questions.correctAnswer: To stay hydrated and keep your body working well
questions.explanation: Drink before you play so you start hydrated, sip during play to replace sweat, and drink after to help your body recover.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: drink water before, during, and after play!

questions.question: What is the best way to get stronger?
questions.correctAnswer: Regular exercise with rest days in between
distractors: Exercising as hard as possible every day
questions.explanation: Muscles grow stronger with regular work plus rest.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: work out regularly and rest - muscles grow stronger!

questions.question: How can walking to school help your health?
questions.correctAnswer: It adds physical activity to your day
distractors: It makes you tired for class
It does not help at all
questions.explanation: Walking makes your heart and legs work, and every step counts toward the 60 minutes of activity kids need each day.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: walking to school is free exercise!

questions.question: What is flexibility?
questions.correctAnswer: How well your muscles and joints can bend and stretch
distractors: How much weight you can lift
How long you can hold your breath
questions.explanation: Flexibility is the range of motion in your joints.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: flexibility is how bendy you are!

questions.question: Why do you need rest days after hard exercise?
questions.correctAnswer: Muscles need time to recover and grow stronger
questions.explanation: Rest lets muscles repair and get stronger.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: rest days let muscles rebuild stronger!

questions.question: What is a healthy way to handle feeling angry?
questions.correctAnswer: Take deep breaths and talk about it calmly
questions.explanation: Deep breaths and calm words help anger pass safely.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: breathe deep, talk calm - anger passes!

questions.question: What should you do if you feel sad for a long time?
questions.correctAnswer: Talk to a trusted adult, like a parent or teacher
distractors: Pretend it will go away on its own
questions.explanation: Trusted adults can help when sadness lasts a long time.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: sad for a long time means tell a trusted adult!

questions.question: What is empathy?
questions.correctAnswer: Understanding how someone else feels
questions.explanation: Empathy means putting yourself in someone else's shoes.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: empathy is feeling with someone else!

questions.question: What is a good way to make a new friend?
questions.correctAnswer: Be kind, listen, and include them
questions.explanation: Kindness and inclusion build friendships.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: kindness and listening make friends!

questions.question: What should you do if you see someone being bullied?
questions.correctAnswer: Tell a trusted adult and support the person being bullied
questions.explanation: Telling an adult and being kind to the victim helps stop bullying.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: see bullying? Tell an adult and be kind!

questions.question: What is bullying?
questions.correctAnswer: Repeated unkind behavior meant to hurt or scare someone
questions.explanation: Bullying is repeated, on purpose, and unfair.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: bullying is repeated meanness on purpose!

questions.question: What is a good way to calm down when you feel worried?
questions.correctAnswer: Take slow, deep breaths
questions.explanation: Slow breathing calms your body and mind.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: slow breaths calm worried minds!

questions.question: Why is it important to talk about your feelings?
questions.correctAnswer: Talking helps you understand feelings and get support
questions.explanation: Sharing feelings helps you cope and lets others help.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: talking about feelings helps you feel better!

questions.question: What does it mean to be resilient?
questions.correctAnswer: To bounce back after a hard time
questions.explanation: Resilience means recovering and trying again after setbacks.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: resilience is bouncing back after a tough time!

questions.question: What is a growth mindset?
questions.correctAnswer: Believing you can improve by practicing and learning
distractors: Believing you are born smart or not
questions.explanation: A growth mindset says effort and learning make you better.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: practice grows your brain - growth mindset!

questions.question: What should you do if a friend tells you a secret that someone is getting hurt?
questions.correctAnswer: Tell a trusted adult right away
distractors: Keep it secret no matter what
questions.explanation: Safety comes first: an adult needs to know if someone is hurt.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: if someone is hurt, tell an adult - secrets cannot hide danger!

questions.question: Why is it important to spend time with friends and family?
questions.correctAnswer: Close relationships support your happiness and health
questions.explanation: Good relationships help you feel loved and supported.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: friends and family keep your heart happy!

questions.question: What is a good way to handle a disagreement with a friend?
questions.correctAnswer: Listen, talk calmly, and try to understand each other
questions.explanation: Calm listening and talking solve disagreements.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: listen first, talk calmly, solve it together!

questions.question: What can you do to feel better after a bad day?
questions.correctAnswer: Do something you enjoy, like reading or playing outside
questions.explanation: Healthy activities help bad feelings pass.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: a favorite activity can turn a bad day around!

questions.question: What is self-confidence?
questions.correctAnswer: Believing in yourself and your abilities
distractors: Thinking you are better than everyone
questions.explanation: Self-confidence means trusting yourself to try and learn.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: confidence is trusting yourself to try!

questions.question: What should you do first if someone is bleeding from a small cut?
questions.correctAnswer: Press a clean cloth on it and wash it with soap and water
questions.explanation: Pressing slows the bleeding, and washing with soap and water removes dirt and germs. Cover it with a bandage to keep it clean.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: clean it, press it, cover it!

questions.question: What should you do if someone has a nosebleed?
questions.correctAnswer: Lean forward and pinch the soft part of the nose
distractors: Lean back and tilt your head up
questions.explanation: Leaning forward and pinching helps the bleeding stop.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: lean forward and pinch gently for a nosebleed!

questions.question: What should you do if you get a small burn?
questions.correctAnswer: Cool it with running water
questions.explanation: Cool running water lowers the skin's temperature and eases pain. Never use ice or butter - they can hurt the skin more.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: cool water soothes a small burn!

questions.question: When should you call 911?
questions.correctAnswer: In an emergency, like a serious injury or someone who cannot breathe
questions.explanation: 911 is for real emergencies only.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: 911 is for real emergencies!

questions.question: What should you do if you find medicine on the ground?
questions.correctAnswer: Leave it alone and tell an adult
distractors: Taste it to see what it is
questions.explanation: Medicine can be dangerous; only adults should handle it.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: unknown medicine means tell an adult - never taste it!

questions.question: Why should you only take medicine from a trusted adult?
questions.correctAnswer: Medicine can be harmful if you take the wrong kind or amount
distractors: Adults like to be in charge
questions.explanation: The wrong medicine or dose can make you very sick.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: medicine is only safe when an adult gives the right dose!

questions.question: What should you do if you smell smoke or see a fire?
questions.correctAnswer: Get out quickly and tell an adult or call 911
distractors: Try to put out a big fire yourself
questions.explanation: Get out fast and get help; never hide.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: fire means get out fast and get help!

questions.question: What is the stop, drop, and roll technique for?
questions.correctAnswer: If your clothes catch fire
questions.explanation: Stop, drop, and roll smothers flames on clothing.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: stop, drop, and roll puts out flames on clothes!

questions.question: Why should you never play with matches or lighters?
questions.correctAnswer: They can start a fire that hurts people
questions.explanation: Matches and lighters can start dangerous fires.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: matches and lighters are tools for adults only!

questions.question: What is tobacco?
questions.correctAnswer: A plant used to make cigarettes, which harms the lungs
questions.explanation: Tobacco smoke damages lungs and causes disease.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: tobacco smoke harms your lungs!

questions.question: What does alcohol do to a child's body?
questions.correctAnswer: It can harm the growing brain and body
questions.explanation: Alcohol is harmful for kids and can damage the brain.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: alcohol harms growing brains and bodies!

questions.question: What should you do if someone offers you a cigarette or alcohol?
questions.correctAnswer: Say no and tell a trusted adult
questions.explanation: Cigarettes and alcohol can harm a growing body. Saying no and telling an adult keeps you safe from pressure to try them.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: just say no and tell an adult!

questions.question: What is peer pressure?
questions.correctAnswer: When others try to get you to do something you do not want to do
distractors: When you play a team sport
questions.explanation: Peer pressure pushes you toward choices that may be unsafe.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: peer pressure is others pushing you to do things!

questions.question: Why is it important to know what is in your food and drinks?
questions.correctAnswer: So you can avoid things that are unsafe or unhealthy
distractors: So you can share with friends
questions.explanation: Knowing ingredients helps you make safe choices.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: know what is in it before you eat or drink it!

questions.question: What should you do if you feel sick at school?
questions.correctAnswer: Tell your teacher right away
distractors: Go home alone without telling anyone
questions.explanation: Your teacher can take you to the nurse and call your parent. Hiding it can let a small problem get worse.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: feeling sick means tell your teacher right away!

questions.question: What is a first aid kit?
questions.correctAnswer: A box with supplies like bandages for treating small injuries
questions.explanation: A first aid kit holds bandages, antiseptic, and other basics.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: a first aid kit is the helper box for small injuries!

questions.question: What should you do if a classmate falls and cannot get up?
questions.correctAnswer: Stay calm, get an adult, and do not move them if they are badly hurt
questions.explanation: Get an adult fast and avoid moving someone who may be hurt.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: stay calm, get an adult, do not move them!

questions.question: Why should you wear a seatbelt in a car?
questions.correctAnswer: It keeps you safe if the car stops suddenly or crashes
distractors: It makes the car go faster
questions.explanation: Seatbelts hold you in place and prevent serious injury.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: buckle up - a seatbelt saves lives!

questions.question: What does SPF on sunscreen mean?
questions.correctAnswer: It shows how much protection the sunscreen gives from sunburn
distractors: It is the size of the bottle
questions.explanation: Higher SPF means more protection from UV rays.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: SPF is the sun protection number!

questions.question: What is the most important thing to remember about safety?
questions.correctAnswer: Tell a trusted adult when something feels wrong or unsafe
distractors: Safety is only for little kids
questions.explanation: Parents, teachers, and other trusted adults know how to help in danger. Telling them quickly is the safest first step.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: when something feels unsafe, tell a trusted adult!

questions.question: What does consent mean when it comes to your body and personal space?
questions.correctAnswer: Asking permission first and getting a clear yes - and respecting the answer
distractors: Doing something as long as no one finds out
Assuming it is okay if the other person does not say anything
Asking once and then doing it anyway, even if the answer is no
questions.explanation: Consent means asking permission and listening to the answer. A clear yes means it is okay, and a no - or no answer at all - means it is not. Maryland law requires schools to teach the meaning of consent and respect for personal boundaries (Education Article section 7-445).
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: consent means ask first, and a clear yes is the only yes!

questions.question: If someone said yes to a hug or a game, can they change their mind later?
questions.correctAnswer: Yes - a person can change their mind at any time, and everyone must respect that right away
distractors: No - once someone says yes, they can never change their mind
Only if a teacher says they can
Only at the end of the day
questions.explanation: Consent can be taken back at any time. If someone changes their mind, the kind and respectful thing to do is to stop right away - no arguing and no trying to change their mind back.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: a yes can become a no at any time - and no always wins!

questions.question: What is a personal boundary?
questions.correctAnswer: A limit that protects your body, your space, and your feelings - and other people must respect it
distractors: A rule that only teachers have to follow
A line you may cross whenever you want
questions.explanation: Personal boundaries are the limits each person sets for their own body, space, and feelings. Everyone has them, everyone deserves to have theirs respected, and respecting other people's boundaries is part of being kind and safe.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: boundaries are invisible lines that keep everyone respected!

questions.question: Which parts of your body are private body parts?
questions.correctAnswer: The parts covered by a swimsuit - they belong to you, and only a doctor or caregiver helping you stay healthy may touch them
distractors: Your hands and feet are private, so nobody is ever allowed to see them or hold your hand
Your hair and ears are private, so nobody is ever allowed to touch your hair or look at your ears
No parts of the body are private, so anyone can touch any part of your body whenever they want
questions.explanation: The parts of your body covered by a swimsuit are private. They belong to you alone. A doctor or a caregiver helping you stay healthy or clean is the exception - and even then, you can always tell a trusted adult if anything feels confusing or wrong. No one should ask to see them, either.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: the swimsuit rule - those parts are private and belong to you!

questions.question: What makes a touch an unsafe touch?
questions.correctAnswer: A touch that involves private body parts, hurts you, or makes you feel uncomfortable, scared, or confused
distractors: A high five from a friend
A handshake when you meet someone
A hug you asked for and wanted
questions.explanation: Safe touches feel good and are welcome, like a high five or a hug you wanted. Unsafe touches involve private body parts or make you feel uncomfortable, scared, or confused - and you never have to accept them.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: if a touch feels wrong or uncomfortable, it is not okay - trust that feeling!

questions.question: What is the difference between an unsafe secret and a safe surprise?
questions.correctAnswer: An unsafe secret is about touch or makes you feel bad and must never be kept, while a safe surprise is a happy thing shared soon
distractors: There is no difference - all secrets must always be kept, even secrets that make you feel bad or worried
A safe surprise is a secret that you must keep hidden forever and never tell anyone about at all
An unsafe secret is only about birthday gifts, so secrets about touch never need to be told to anyone
questions.explanation: Safe surprises are happy and shared soon. Unsafe secrets are about touch, or make you feel worried, scared, or uncomfortable - and those secrets should never be kept. Always tell a trusted adult about an unsafe secret, even if someone told you not to. A birthday gift is a good example of a safe surprise.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: surprises are happy and shared soon - unsafe secrets are never kept!

questions.question: What are the three safety steps if someone touches you in a way that feels wrong?
questions.correctAnswer: Say no in a firm voice, get away to a safe place, and tell a trusted adult - and keep telling until someone helps
distractors: Stay quiet and hope it stops
Keep it secret so no one gets in trouble
Wait a long time to see if it happens again
questions.explanation: Use the three safety steps: say no, get away, and tell. Go to a safe place and tell a trusted adult what happened. If the first adult does not help, keep telling other trusted adults until someone does. Maryland law requires this safety teaching in school (Education Article section 7-439).
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: say no, get away, and tell - and keep telling until you are helped!

questions.question: If someone hurts a child or touches a child in an unsafe way, whose fault is it?
questions.correctAnswer: Never the child's fault - it is always the fault of the person who did it
distractors: The child's fault for not stopping it
questions.explanation: Abuse is never, ever the child's fault. It does not matter what the child said, did, or wore. The person who chose to hurt or touch a child in an unsafe way is the only one at fault, and telling a trusted adult is always the right thing to do.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: if someone hurts a child, it is never the child's fault - not ever!

questions.question: What is a safe boundary to keep when you are online?
questions.correctAnswer: Do not share personal photos or personal information, and tell a trusted adult right away about any message that feels uncomfortable
distractors: Share your photos with anyone who asks nicely
Keep uncomfortable messages secret from adults
Share your home address so new friends can visit
questions.explanation: Boundaries protect you online too. Never share personal photos, your full name, your address, or your school with people online, and if a message makes you feel uncomfortable or asks you to keep secrets, show it to a trusted adult right away.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: online boundaries count too - no personal photos, and tell an adult about uncomfortable messages!

questions.question: An adult gives a child special gifts and extra attention, asks the child to keep their time together a secret, and slowly tests the child's boundaries. Why is this pattern a warning sign?
questions.correctAnswer: It can be grooming - a way someone slowly makes unsafe behavior seem normal - and the child should tell a trusted adult right away
distractors: It just means the adult is extra friendly, so the child should keep the secrets to be polite
It is only a problem if the adult has already touched the child in an unsafe way
It means the child did something wrong and should try to handle it alone
questions.explanation: Grooming is when someone slowly builds trust and tests boundaries - with special attention, gifts, and secrets - so unsafe behavior starts to feel normal. Recognizing the pattern early helps keep children safe: tell a trusted adult right away. Connecticut law (CGS 17a-101q) requires schools to teach students to recognize grooming and other warning signs.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: special gifts plus secrets plus testing boundaries is a warning pattern - spot it and tell!

questions.question: Your friend tells you that someone has been making them feel uncomfortable and asks you to keep it a secret. What is the best way to help your friend?
questions.correctAnswer: Support your friend, and tell a trusted adult right away - a friend never keeps a secret that could keep someone unsafe
distractors: Promise to keep the secret, because good friends never tell what a friend asked them to hide
Try to handle it alone by confronting the person yourself
Wait and do nothing unless your friend brings it up again
questions.explanation: A bystander is someone who sees or hears that something is wrong and chooses to help. Believe and support your friend, and tell a trusted adult right away - even if your friend asked you to keep it secret. Unsafe secrets are never kept, and telling an adult is how friends protect each other. Connecticut's statewide safety program teaches students to help as bystanders (CGS 17a-101q).
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: a good friend never keeps an unsafe secret - support your friend and tell a trusted adult!

questions.question: A child tells a trusted adult about unsafe behavior, but worries that telling was wrong because someone might get in trouble. What should the child remember?
questions.correctAnswer: Telling is always the right and brave thing to do - it is never the child's fault, and if one adult does not help, keep telling other trusted adults until someone does
distractors: Telling was a mistake if it gets someone in trouble, so the child should take it back
The child should feel ashamed, because speaking up causes problems for everyone
One try is enough - if the first adult does not help, the child should stop telling
questions.explanation: Telling is never wrong. A child who speaks up is brave, and unsafe behavior is never the child's fault - not ever. If the first adult does not listen or help, keep telling other trusted adults until someone does help. Connecticut law (CGS 17a-101q) requires schools to teach that disclosure - telling a trusted adult - is how children get help and stay safe.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: telling is brave and always right - and keep telling until someone helps!

questions.question: In Nevada, schools teach personal safety in health class. What is the main reason for these lessons?
questions.correctAnswer: So every child knows how to recognize danger and get help from a responsible adult
distractors: So children can handle every dangerous situation completely on their own
So children learn to keep safety problems private
So adults no longer need to watch out for children's safety
questions.explanation: Nevada law (NRS 389.064) requires personal-safety instruction as part of a health course of study. The lessons teach children to recognize hazards - including danger from unsafe people - and to report threats of harm to a responsible adult.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Safety lessons have one goal: spot danger early and get a grown-up's help!

questions.question: You are shopping with your family and realize you are lost in a big store. What is the safest thing to do?
questions.correctAnswer: Stay where you are or go to a store worker at a register and tell them you are lost, so they can find your adult
distractors: Leave the store and walk to the parking lot to look for your family's car
Hide so nobody can see you until your family walks past
Follow any friendly shopper who offers to take you outside
questions.explanation: Nevada's personal-safety standards include what to do when a child becomes lost or separated. Staying in a safe public place and asking a worker - someone in uniform or at a register - for help keeps you where your adult can find you.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Lost? Stay put, find a worker, and let help come to you!

img.scene: A child standing calmly beside a checkout counter speaking with a store worker in uniform, bright supermarket aisles behind. No readable text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: T-Rexy says: Lost? Stay put, find a worker, and let help come to you!
img.title: LOST IN THE STORE

questions.question: A person you have never met stops near the park and offers you a ride home, saying your parent sent them. What should you do?
questions.correctAnswer: Do not get in - move away, stay with other people, and tell a responsible adult right away
distractors: Get in, because the person knew your parent's name
Ask the person to drive slowly so you can jump out
Go with them only if they seem friendly and smile a lot
questions.explanation: An unsafe person can be a stranger: no adult your family truly sent will mind if you check first. Refuse, create distance, and report the approach to a responsible adult - Nevada's safety lessons name danger from unsafe persons you do not know.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: A surprise pickup is a red flag - check first, always!

img.scene: A child stepping back toward a group of families on a park path while a car waits at the curb with its door closed, trees and a playground behind. No readable text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: T-Rexy says: A surprise pickup is a red flag - check first, always!

questions.question: During a game, a babysitter keeps tickling you after you say stop, and laughs that you are being too serious. What is happening, and what can you do?
questions.correctAnswer: Your stop was not respected - you can move away, say no clearly, and tell a parent or another responsible adult
distractors: Tickling is always safe, so you should just laugh along
You must be wrong about feeling uncomfortable
You should tickle the babysitter back until they stop
questions.explanation: Unsafe behavior can come from a person you know, not only strangers. When someone ignores a clear stop about your body, that is a boundary being broken - moving away and telling a responsible adult is exactly what Nevada's personal-safety instruction teaches.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Stop means stop - even from someone you know!

img.scene: A child holding up a hand in a clear stop gesture and stepping toward an open doorway where a parent is arriving home, living room setting. No readable text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: T-Rexy says: Stop means stop - even from someone you know!
img.title: STOP MEANS STOP

questions.question: You are at a neighbor's house and something there makes you feel unsafe. You said you want to leave, but the adult says you must stay and keep it between you two. What is the best action?
questions.correctAnswer: Leave to a safe place if you can, and tell your parent or another responsible adult as soon as possible - an adult who demands secrecy about safety is a warning sign
distractors: Stay, because children must always obey every adult in their house
Keep the secret, since the adult asked you to
Wait a few weeks to see if it happens again before telling anyone
questions.explanation: Demanding secrecy about something unsafe is itself a danger sign. Nevada's personal-safety standards teach children to get to safety and report threats of harm to a responsible adult - no adult's instruction to hide a safety problem overrides that.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Secrecy plus unsafe is a double red flag - get out and tell!

img.scene: A child walking out of a front door toward their own home across the street where a parent waits on the porch, late afternoon light. No readable text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: T-Rexy says: Secrecy plus unsafe is a double red flag - get out and tell!
img.title: GET OUT AND TELL

questions.question: Someone you met in an online game, who says they are your age, asks for a photo of you and your home address so they can 'visit'. What should you do?
questions.correctAnswer: Do not send anything - end the chat and tell a parent or another responsible adult, because you cannot know who is really typing
distractors: Send the photo but not the address, as a fair compromise
Ask them to send their address first, then decide
Share your location only if they promise to keep it secret
questions.explanation: Online, an unsafe person can pretend to be a child. Asking for photos or a home address is a recognized danger sign, and the safe response is to stop contact and report it to a responsible adult right away.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: You cannot see who is typing - so never send photos or addresses!

img.scene: A child closing a laptop at a kitchen table and turning to speak with a parent standing nearby, a game controller resting unused beside the laptop. No readable text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: T-Rexy says: You cannot see who is typing - so never send photos or addresses!

questions.question: You told one trusted adult about unsafe behavior, but that adult was busy and did not really listen. What should you do next?
questions.correctAnswer: Keep telling - go to another trusted adult, like a teacher, school counselor, or family member, until someone listens and helps
distractors: Give up, because telling once is all you are supposed to do
Decide the problem must not be important after all
Try to fix the problem by yourself instead
questions.explanation: Reporting works when you keep going: if one adult does not respond, tell another. Nevada's personal-safety instruction names reporting threats of harm to a responsible adult - and a child's job is to keep telling until an adult acts.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: One adult did not listen? Tell the next one - keep telling!

img.scene: A child speaking with a school counselor in a warm office, a teacher waiting kindly in the doorway behind them. No readable text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: T-Rexy says: One adult did not listen? Tell the next one - keep telling!

questions.question: After a child reports unsafe behavior, what should happen - and what do helpers want the child to know?
questions.correctAnswer: Adults should act to protect the child and get support - reporting brings help, and the child is never in trouble for telling
distractors: The child will be punished for causing problems
Nothing changes, because reports are kept secret from everyone
The child must prove everything alone before anyone may help
questions.explanation: Victim assistance is part of the safety system: counselors, trusted adults and protective services exist to help a child who reports. Telling brings protection and support - it never makes the reporting child the one in trouble.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Telling brings help, never punishment - helpers are on your side!

img.scene: A school counselor and a parent sitting supportively on either side of a child on a bench outside a school office, calm and reassuring. No readable text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: T-Rexy says: Telling brings help, never punishment - helpers are on your side!
img.title: TELLING BRINGS HELP

questions.question: Before taking a photo of a classmate and sharing it with the class group chat, what does consent ask you to do?
questions.correctAnswer: Ask your classmate first, and share the photo only if they clearly agree - and remove it if they later ask you to
distractors: Share it quickly before they can object
Share it if everyone else in the chat already has it
Ask a different classmate for permission instead
questions.explanation: Consent applies to everyday respect, not only emergencies: a person's image belongs to them, permission can be refused, and a yes can be withdrawn. Asking first and honoring the answer is the boundary Nevada's safety lessons build on.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Their photo, their choice - ask before you share!

img.scene: A pupil holding a tablet camera lowered at their side, asking a classmate a question in a school hallway while the classmate smiles and nods. No readable text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: T-Rexy says: Their photo, their choice - ask before you share!
img.title: ASK BEFORE YOU SHARE

questions.question: Some adults try to trick kids by offering gifts, rides or treats to get them to go somewhere or keep a secret. What is the safest thing to do?
questions.correctAnswer: Say no, walk away, and tell a trusted adult right away
distractors: Accept the gift if the person seems friendly
Go along, but only for a short time
Keep it secret so you do not hurt their feelings
questions.explanation: Tricking a child with gifts or rides is a warning sign of trafficking and abuse - adults who are safe do not ask children to keep secrets or go places alone with them. Walking away and telling a trusted adult is always the right move, and it is never the child's fault.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Gifts with secrets are a trap - walk away and tell.

img.scene: A child walking toward a school entrance where a teacher waits, bright daylight, safe mood. No readable text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: T-Rexy says: Gifts with secrets are a trap - walk away and tell.

questions.question: During an online game, another player starts asking where you live and wants you to send a picture of yourself. What is the safe response?
questions.correctAnswer: Never send it - close the chat and tell a trusted adult
distractors: Send the photo but not the address
Send it if they sent you a photo first
Ask them to promise to keep it secret, then send it
questions.explanation: Strangers online who ask children for photos or addresses may be traffickers building trust to lure a child. The safe answer is always no: stop, close the chat, and tell a trusted adult - even if the person seemed kind.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Online strangers asking for photos: stop and tell.

img.scene: A tablet on a desk with a blank chat screen, a parent's hand resting supportively beside it. No readable text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: T-Rexy says: Online strangers asking for photos: stop and tell.

questions.question: What does the word trafficking mean when adults talk about keeping kids safe?
questions.correctAnswer: Tricking, forcing or pressuring someone - even a child - into doing work or things they do not want to do, so someone else gains from it
distractors: Directing cars at a busy intersection
A traffic jam on the highway
questions.explanation: Human trafficking means a person is tricked, threatened or forced into labor or harmful acts for someone else's benefit. It can happen in any town, it often starts with gifts, promises or online messages, and it is never the victim's fault.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Trafficking is tricking and forcing - never the victim's fault.

img.scene: A caring school counselor's office with a warm lamp and comfortable chairs, calm and safe. No readable text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: T-Rexy says: Trafficking is tricking and forcing - never the victim's fault.
img.title: WHAT TRAFFICKING MEANS

questions.question: Someone you know - not a stranger - keeps asking you to keep your meetings secret and gives you presents. Why is this a warning sign?
questions.correctAnswer: Safe adults do not build secret, gift-giving relationships with children - secrecy and gifts are tools traffickers use to gain control
distractors: It is only a warning sign if the person is a stranger
Presents always mean the person is dangerous
Secrets between adults and kids are fine if the gifts are small
questions.explanation: Most harm to children comes from people the child knows. Secret meetings and special gifts are classic grooming steps: they make a child feel chosen and then trapped. Telling a trusted adult breaks the secrecy that protects the behavior.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Known or stranger, secrets plus gifts mean tell.

img.scene: A child talking with a trusted teacher beside a classroom door, open and well-lit setting. No readable text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: T-Rexy says: Known or stranger, secrets plus gifts mean tell.

questions.question: A new 'friend' online says you are special, listens to all your problems, and now wants to meet in person. What is happening most likely?
questions.correctAnswer: This is a grooming pattern - the person is building trust to lure you, and you should tell a trusted adult and never meet
distractors: You have found a true best friend
Meeting is fine if it is in a public park
It is safe if they say they are your age
questions.explanation: Traffickers pose as peers or caring friends online, shower a child with attention, and then push for a meeting or photos. A trusted adult needs to know right away; no online friend should ever ask a child to meet in secret.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Too-perfect online friends are a lure - tell an adult.

img.scene: A phone lying face-down on a family kitchen table, warm home light, safe mood. No readable text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: T-Rexy says: Too-perfect online friends are a lure - tell an adult.

questions.question: If a kid has been tricked or forced by a trafficker, whose fault is it?
questions.correctAnswer: Never the kid's fault - the trafficker is always to blame, and telling brings help, not punishment
distractors: The kid's fault for trusting the person
questions.explanation: Arkansas law (section 6-16-157) requires schools to teach exactly this: victims are never to blame. Children who tell get protection and help. Shame is the trafficker's tool; speaking up is how it loses power.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Victim is never to blame - telling brings help.

img.tip: T-Rexy says: Victim is never to blame - telling brings help.

questions.question: Which of these is a trafficking danger sign a 5th grader should report to a trusted adult?
questions.correctAnswer: An older teen or adult offers you money, a phone or a place to stay if you will 'help with errands' and not tell anyone
distractors: A teacher schedules a parent meeting
A coach posts the practice schedule
A librarian recommends a book series
questions.explanation: Offers of money, phones, shelter or jobs - paired with secrecy - are recruitment tools, even when aimed at older kids and teens. Any of them should be reported, whether they happen to you or to a friend.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Money, phones and secrecy offered together: report it.

questions.question: Your friend tells you an adult online is sending her gifts and asking her not to tell her parents. What is the best way to help?
questions.correctAnswer: Tell a trusted adult yourself - helping a friend means breaking the secret, even if she asked you not to
distractors: Promise to keep her secret no matter what
Wait and see if it gets worse
Message the adult and tell him to stop
questions.explanation: Secrets that protect an adult's access to a child must be broken. Telling a trusted adult is not betraying a friend - it is the strongest protection a friend can give, and adults can then involve people whose job is stopping trafficking.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Break the secret to protect your friend.

questions.question: Why do Arkansas schools teach students about trafficking at every grade level?
questions.correctAnswer: State law (section 6-16-157) requires a sequential K-12 program on detecting, preventing and getting help for child abuse and human trafficking, because traffickers target children and prevention works
distractors: Because trafficking only happens in other countries
Because students asked for extra homework
Because it is part of the driving test
questions.explanation: Arkansas Code section 6-16-157 orders the state to build K-12 materials on the detection, intervention, prevention and treatment of child sexual abuse and human trafficking, and every district must teach a prevention program. Traffickers target minors - including through phones - so the lessons grow with the student.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Arkansas teaches it K-12 because prevention works.

questions.question: What is sexual extortion?
questions.correctAnswer: It is when someone threatens to share private or embarrassing pictures or information unless the victim sends more pictures, money, or does what the person demands
distractors: A game children play online with friends
When a website charges money for games
questions.explanation: Sexual extortion is a form of abuse and a crime: a person - sometimes pretending to be a kid - tricks or pressures a child into sharing private images, then threatens to share them unless the child obeys. Delaware's Erin's Law (14 Del. C. section 4163) requires teaching students about it.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Extortion means threats - it is never the victim's fault.

questions.question: What is the safest rule about pictures of your body or private information online?
questions.correctAnswer: Never create or share private pictures of yourself online, and never share them because someone asks, pressures, or threatens you
distractors: Share pictures only with people who promise to delete them
Share pictures if the person sends one first
It is safe if you use a disappearing-messages app
questions.explanation: No app makes a shared image truly private - screenshots last forever. Erin's Law online-safety teaching is simple: never create or send private images, and pressure or promises are warning signs to stop and tell a trusted adult.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Never create it, never send it.

questions.question: If someone online threatens to share a private picture of you unless you send more, what should you do FIRST?
questions.correctAnswer: Stop replying, save the messages if you can, and tell a trusted adult right away - it is a crime against you, and adults and police can help
distractors: Send what they ask so they stop
Delete everything and never tell anyone
Pay them money so they go away
questions.explanation: Victims of sexual extortion should never comply or pay - demands grow. Stop contact, keep the evidence, and tell a trusted adult immediately; reporting protects the victim and can stop the offender. Help is available through trusted adults, school counselors, and law enforcement.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Stop, save, tell - help stops the threats.
